title: Mortgage Loan File Compliance Manual: TRID Tolerance Buckets and Cure Delivery
content:
**§1 Comparison at closing.** The clause "At closing the charges on the final Closing Disclosure are compared with the good-faith baseline (the initial Loan Estimate, or the latest timely revised Loan Estimate whose changed circumstance affected the charge)" is no longer in force for the zero-tolerance bucket before consummation, and only for it. The 10 percent bucket, and any violation found only after consummation, are still compared on the final Closing Disclosure with the good-faith baseline (the initial Loan Estimate, or the latest timely revised Loan Estimate whose changed circumstance affected the charge).

**§2 Zero-tolerance bucket.** The clause "In the zero-tolerance bucket the cure is the amount by which the zero-tolerance total on the Closing Disclosure exceeds the baseline zero-tolerance total" is no longer in force for the zero-tolerance cure measured before consummation. A zero-tolerance violation found only after consummation is still the amount by which the zero-tolerance total on the final Closing Disclosure exceeds the baseline zero-tolerance total.

| Comparison | Basis in force here |
|---|---|
| 10 percent bucket | final Closing Disclosure against the good-faith baseline (§1, §3) |
| Zero-tolerance violation found only after consummation | final Closing Disclosure zero-tolerance total over the baseline zero-tolerance total (§1, §2) |
| Zero-tolerance bucket before consummation | §1 and §2 are no longer in force for it |

**§3 Ten percent bucket.** In the 10 percent bucket of a Mortgage Loan File the cure is the amount by which the 10 percent bucket total on the Closing Disclosure exceeds the baseline 10 percent bucket total increased by the program's 10 percent tolerance percentage, rounded to the cent.

**§4 No netting; uncapped charges.** A decrease in either bucket is never netted against an increase in the other, and charges with no tolerance limit (prepaid interest, insurance premiums, services the borrower shopped for outside the provider list) are never cured.

**§5 Delivery of a cure.** A cure known before consummation is given as a lender credit on the Closing Disclosure (a credit at closing); a violation found later is refunded with a corrected Closing Disclosure (a post-closing refund).

**§6 Post-closing refund window.** A post-closing tolerance refund must be paid no later than the end of the cure window that starts on the consummation date. Calendar days are counted forward from the file's closed date (the consummation date), which is day zero; a refund paid on the last day of the window is timely. The window is the program's cure refund period in calendar days. The evidence is the closed date recorded on the file.

**§7 Payment.** Each payment names the assessed cure it pays and pays it in full.

## Ten percent bucket, worked through (hypothetical figures, 10.00 percent tolerance)

| Baseline 10 percent bucket total | Closing Disclosure 10 percent bucket total | Baseline increased by 10.00 percent | Cure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1800.00 USD | 1950.00 USD | 1980.00 USD | none — 1950.00 does not exceed 1980.00 |
| 1800.00 USD | 2015.25 USD | 1980.00 USD | 35.25 USD |
| 1234.56 USD | 1400.00 USD | 1358.016, rounded to 1358.02 USD | 41.98 USD |

## Post-consummation zero-tolerance violation (hypothetical figures)

A zero-tolerance violation found only after consummation, where the final Closing Disclosure shows a zero-tolerance total of 3100.00 USD against a baseline zero-tolerance total of 2972.30 USD, is 127.70 USD, refunded with a corrected Closing Disclosure within the refund window.

## Refund window, worked through (hypothetical, 60-day window)

A loan consummated on 10 April (day zero) has a window whose last day is 9 June; a refund paid on 9 June is timely and one paid on 10 June is not.
